title: The Space Security Landscape Is Deteriorating Rapidly
author: Rajeswari Pillai Rajagopalan
text:
Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink delivers a keynote address during the 2026 Air, Space & Cyber Conference at the National Harbor, Md., Sept 14, 2026.
Credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth
There is little doubt that great power competition is ramping up. Now, another front has opened, with the United States announcing that it has deployed a space weapon. China, and subsequently Russia, had been pushing the limits in space, testing advanced technologies with possible offensive uses in outer space, including cyber weapons, ground-based lasers, and artificial robotic arms that could be used for repairing satellites but also have obvious military and intelligence uses. Now the U.S. has responded by joining the developing arms race, which is likely to spur further competition. The space arms race now appears to be fully underway. [...]
